description: CONTRADICTION (high — explicitly identified as a contradiction by the Chairperson on Day 24 confidence, days 22, 24): Lt-Gen Mbotho's and W/O Sabelo Nkosi's Day 24 testimony describes the North West takedown operation as still pending that evening (the reason Nkosi was 'diverted'), while Brigadier Mokoena's earlier testimony (Day 22) had described that operation as already completed with officers returning — a discrepancy the Chairperson flagged and Mbotho could not immediately resolve.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high — both are sworn accounts and the tension was explicitly probed by the evidence leader on Day 20 confidence, days 17, 20): Witness B (Day 17, sworn evidence) characterised the Silverton ballistics report's omissions and later deletion as apparently deliberate interference, while Brig Mkhabela (Day 20, sworn evidence) testified — agreeing with a proposition from the evidence leader — that the paragraph-numbering/omission errors looked more consistent with sloppiness than sabotage, since the flawed report still positively linked the seized firearms to the crime scene.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: A full, redacted transcript of the roughly 5-6 hour Matlala recording (provisional exhibit CJC5.4) was directed to be produced on Day 23 but had not been delivered by day's end; excerpts on Feroz Khan and Shibiri were confirmed to exist but were not played.
would_resolve: Production and public filing of the full transcript.

description: Whether Matlala's numerous bank accounts have been fully analysed remains open; his own affidavit described the analysis as incomplete at the time of deposing (Day 23).
would_resolve: An updated forensic-accounting exhibit.

description: Grounds for Chief Mapiyeye's own September 2024 suspension (referenced only in passing alongside a sexual-harassment matter) were never detailed (Days 27-28).
would_resolve: The suspension letter or disciplinary charge sheet itself.

description: The JMPD officer at the Molefe arrest scene is named 'John Mokgatle' in Day 18's key points, but the same day's unverified notes separately describe a 'JMPD superintendent' identified to the witness as 'Mahomed Hoosen' by the evidence leader — unclear whether these are the same person.
would_resolve: Cross-checking the JMPD officer's affidavit (SDK22, referenced Day 25) against both names.

description: Whether Julius Mkhwanazi was ever actually placed under suspension is not confirmed within the Day 27-30 transcript testimony itself (only that a pre-suspension letter was signed 20 Feb 2023); Tier 2/3 reporting later describes him as on special leave.
would_resolve: A dated HR record or a witness's direct confirmation of the suspension's outcome.

description: The identity of the anonymous emailer(s) alleging City Manager Mashazi protected Julius Mkhwanazi (Annexures RS25/RS26) was never established (Day 30).
would_resolve: Forensic/IP tracing of the email accounts, if pursued by the Commission.

description: Status of several IPID investigations referenced across the record — into cases opened against Witness C's/Khumalo's team, into the Loate/Douglasdale/Katlehong-area cases, and into Julius Mkhwanazi's blue-light conduct — was consistently unknown to the testifying witnesses (Days 17, 23, 27-29).
would_resolve: An IPID case-status update obtained directly from IPID.

description: Whether Lt-Gen Sibiya has SAPS-provided personal protectors was neither confirmed nor denied by Khumalo, who cited TRA classification (Day 25).
would_resolve: A direct answer from Sibiya or a declassified TRA excerpt.

description: The fourth SAPS officer identified in Khumalo's 16 January 2025 cartel-links briefing to Minister Mchunu was withheld from the record, citing an ongoing investigation (Day 26).
would_resolve: Disclosure once that investigation reaches a less sensitive stage.

description: Whether Brigadier Mokoena will be recalled, and how he reconciles his account of the North West operation's status with Mbotho's and Nkosi's, is unresolved (Day 24); his legal advisors have counselled delay pending advice on whether he is an implicated person.
would_resolve: Mokoena's recalled testimony.

description: Why the Bramley/Vereeniging case files were sent to the KZN ballistics lab for a parallel/duplicate analysis was never established; Brig Mkhabela said he learned of it only through Commission proceedings (Days 20-21).
would_resolve: Testimony from whoever authorised the duplicate referral.

description: The basis for Makgotloe's kidnapping complaint (CAS 118/01/2025) against the investigating team, and General Mulaudzi's refusal to give a statement, remain unexplained (Days 17-18).
would_resolve: Makgotloe's or Mulaudzi's testimony, or the outcome of any review of the complaint.

description: Whether Capt/WO Makgotloe's ballistics report errors and the deleted/backdated report versions were negligent or deliberate remains unresolved across Days 17, 20 and 21; Makgotloe has not yet testified.
would_resolve: Makgotloe's own sworn testimony, which the Commission indicated is still to come.

description: The reason SAPS's Cold Case Unit (via Brig Gininda's office and Col Roodt) repeatedly sought the active Vereeniging docket outside normal channels was never established (Day 17).
would_resolve: Testimony from Brigadier Gininda or Colonel Roodt themselves, or a documented request trail.

description: CONTRADICTION (low confidence, days 1, 2): Two figures were given for the dockets removed from the PKTT: 121 on the task team's count and 123 on the head-office audit. Mkhwanazi explained the difference on Day 2 as a counting-rule difference for 'parallel' sub-dockets merged into main dockets. The explanation was accepted and no substantive dispute survived, but the two figures continue to appear interchangeably across later days.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (medium confidence, days 3, 5): Masemola testified on Day 5 that he first became aware of the City of Johannesburg letter questioning Lt Gen Sibiya's suitability only when he saw it on television after Mkhwanazi's Commission testimony — not at the time of Sibiya's appointment or his later promotion to Deputy National Commissioner. The letter itself, introduced by Mkhwanazi on Day 3 as MK23, is dated 20 June 2022 and was addressed to the Minister of Police. Whether the Ministry acted on it, and whether it should have surfaced in the appointment process, was left unresolved; Mkhwanazi could not confirm the date of Sibiya's promotion or who was in office at the time.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (medium confidence, days 2, 7): The PKTT's characterisation of prosecutorial conduct was not borne out. Then-Minister Cele's 24 May 2019 letter to the NDPP (in evidence on Day 2) tabulated 'questionable withdrawal decisions' by KZN prosecutors, and dockets were opened against prosecutors over the manner of those decisions. Adv Harrison testified on Day 7 that a review found the prosecutors' decisions were in fact justified and no disciplinary action was taken. The Chairperson pressed her on what specifically about the 'manner' of the decisions had been objected to; her answer went to a review process not being followed rather than any substantive impropriety.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 5): The Day 5 transcript is internally inconsistent about its own sitting-day number: the cover page reads 'DAY 5' but every running page header throughout the body reads '23 SEPTEMBER 2025 - DAY 4'. This is a defect in the source document rather than a conflict in the evidence, but it affects citation of that day's record.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (medium confidence, days 4, 8, 9, 15): Masemola deferred the 'three envelopes' bribery allegation to another witness on Day 4, describing it as hearsay from his side and saying 'I am sure General Khumalo could talk more on that'. Khumalo did not address the envelopes in his evidence on Days 8 or 9. First-hand evidence of the allegation arrived only on Day 15, from Witness A, who attributed the reference to Maj-Gen Shibiri — a different source from the one Masemola had pointed the Commission to.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 2, 3, 5, 9): Minister Mchunu denied knowing Brown Mogotsi at the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on 5 March 2025, and per Masemola repeated that denial afterwards to Masemola and Deputy Ministers Mathale and Boshielo. Against that denial stand Mkhwanazi's Day 2 allegation that the Minister acknowledged Mogotsi as a 'comrade' in a recorded private call, and the Day 9 Signal messages from Mogotsi to a contact saved on his phone as 'Senzo Mchunu'. The underlying fact remains untested: Mkhwanazi conceded on Day 3 that he cannot confirm the saved contact is the Minister because neither phone had been examined by investigators.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 5): Two opposed accounts of the President's position on disbandment sit in Masemola's Day 5 evidence. Masemola relayed the Minister's assertion that the President was in agreement that the PKTT be disbanded; Masemola immediately contradicted it from his own knowledge, testifying that when he briefed the President on 1 February 2025 the President was 'quite taken aback' to learn the team was being disbanded with no reasons given, and said he would speak to the Minister. Masemola noted of the Minister's claim, 'it is him saying it. So I would not know whether what he is saying is true or not.'
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 8): Khumalo's PKTT 'success' statistics do not reconcile arithmetically. The Chairperson pointed out that adding the 34 'not guilty' outcomes to the 82 'withdrawn' outcomes gives 116, against only 83 convictions, and asked how the figures support the claimed success rate. The witness acknowledged the presentation understated nuance (multiple accused per case) and needed to be more detailed, but no corrected figures were produced within Days 1-15.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (medium confidence, days 5, 8): Lt-Gen Khumalo testified on Day 8 that from the PKTT's point of view 'we have not received any official complaint', attributing criticism to media allegations only. That sits uneasily with Masemola's Day 5 evidence listing repeated complaints by Prof Mary De Haas, and with Commissioner Baloyi's Day 8 question putting the former Sergeant Dlamini matter — a complaint about PKTT conduct that led to a criminal conviction — directly to Khumalo. Khumalo treated the Dlamini matter as an internal employer-employee issue rather than a complaint, and the tension was not fully reconciled.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 4, 8): Minister Mchunu's 31 December 2024 letter states the PKTT was established following the Moerane Commission report. Masemola testified on Day 4 that this is factually wrong — 'This team was not established as a result of the Moerane Commission' — since the Moerane report came out in September 2018 and the team was already in place because of the murders. Khumalo's Day 8 evidence is to the same effect, that the PKTT predated the Moerane findings. Masemola said he does not know the source of the claim in the Minister's letter.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (medium confidence, days 1, 2, 7): The record carries two different sets of dates for the physical removal of the PKTT dockets to Pretoria. Adv Motau SC's Day 1 opening timeline and Mkhwanazi's evidence give 26 March 2025 (118 dockets to Lt Gen Senthumule) and 10 April 2025 (a further 3 dockets), totalling 121. On Day 7 Adv Chaskalson SC put to Adv Harrison that the dockets went 'in two stages on the 28th of March and the 22nd of April' and she answered 'That is correct'. The 22 April date coincides with Sibiya's follow-up letter directing that the transfer be finalised by 24 April, so the two accounts may be conflating letter dates with handover dates, but they were never reconciled on the record.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 3, 5, 6): Lt Gen Sibiya's 4 February 2025 letter to Lt Gen Senthumule states that he was acting on the instruction of the Minister of Police in disbanding the Task Team and determining what should happen to its dockets. The National Commissioner's affidavit in Sibiya's own Pretoria High Court application (Case No 123874/2025) states the handover of dockets was done without the National Commissioner's authority, and Masemola testified he never authorised it. Van Rooyen's statement flags this conflict expressly and does not resolve it.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 5): Masemola initially told the Commission there had been an 'agreement' at the 6 March 2025 Cape Town meeting that dockets should go to their stations of origin. Under sustained questioning from the Chairperson he corrected himself: he and the Deputy National Commissioner for Policing had favoured the KZN Murder and Robbery Unit, the Minister and Chief of Staff Nkabinde overruled that view, and the correct characterisation was the Minister's 'preferred course', not an agreement.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 4): Masemola's own witness statement carries two incompatible characterisations of the same allegation against Lt Gen Sibiya. Paragraph 121 states as apparent fact that Sibiya 'was included as one of the senior SAPS officers involved with criminal syndicate'; paragraph 179.5 describes the same allegations as 'unsubstantiated' and requiring further criminal investigation. Under Adv Motau SC's questioning Masemola directed the Commission to treat 179.5 as the operative version; Commissioner Baloyi noted the two versions may not be strictly reconcilable.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: CONTRADICTION (high confidence, days 4): Lt Gen Masemola testified early on Day 4 that he would categorically refuse any Ministerial instruction straying into operational matters ('if it is clear that it is not his, then I will not obey it'), yet later the same day accepted the Minister's disbandment instruction in a modified, phased form. The Chairperson put the inconsistency to him directly ('But you yourself had actually relented') and Masemola conceded he had relented in substance, while maintaining the PKTT had never in fact been disbanded.
would_resolve: Re-reading the relevant transcript passages side by side, or the commission's own resolution of the point.

description: The evidentiary basis for treating certain WhatsApp messages as forwarded was not examined on the record. The Chairperson questioned how the Commission could tell a message was forwarded when the display software did not flag forwarding as the application normally does; the Evidence Leader explained reliance on a separate metadata spreadsheet that was not itself examined in the hearing. Commissioner Baloyi separately noted on Day 15 that WhatsApp exhibit captions attributing messages to particular senders were not clearly corroborated by the message bodies.
would_resolve: Examination of the extraction metadata and a systematic explanation of the annexure numbering and attribution methodology, which Adv Segeels-Ncube was asked on Day 15 to provide.

description: The status and outcome of several parallel processes referenced in evidence are unknown to the witnesses: the IDAC investigation into the referred dockets; the IPID investigation into the Minister's alleged interference complaint in the Empangeni matter; the DPCI Head appointment process after the advertised post was withdrawn; and the charge sheet for Lt Gen Sibiya's disciplinary hearing, which Masemola said he deliberately does not know in order to preserve the neutrality of that process.
would_resolve: Status reports from IDAC, IPID and SAPS Human Resources, and the disciplinary charge sheet once served.

description: The Day 6 record consists solely of Major-General van Rooyen's written statement and annexures VR1-VR9. It contains no oral hearing transcript — no Chairperson dialogue and no examination — so whether her legal opinion that the directive was unlawful executive overreach was orally led, questioned or tested on that sitting day cannot be established from the record. Her statement also closes with a note that a further statement may follow, which does not appear in Days 7 to 15.
would_resolve: The oral transcript for the 25 September 2025 sitting, if one exists, and the further statement her statement foreshadows.

description: Whether the Minister's directive was ever actually implemented as to personnel, as distinct from dockets, was asked by Commissioner Khumalo SC on Day 1 and expressly deferred. Across Days 2 to 9 the position remained that no witness had sent a disbandment instruction onward, that the team continued operating with reduced personnel reportedly for budgetary reasons, and that the team had never in fact been disbanded — yet Sibiya's 4 February 2025 letter directed deactivation and disbandment. The operative status of the team through 2025 is not clearly established.
would_resolve: Establishment records, personnel postings and budget approvals for the PKTT across 2025, and evidence from Lt Gen Sibiya and Lt Gen Senthumule on what was done in consequence of the letters.

description: The docket figures and removal dates remain unreconciled across the record: 121 on the task team's count against 123 on the head-office audit, and removal on 26 March and 10 April per Days 1 and 2 against 28 March and 22 April per Day 7. It is also unresolved what proportion of the dockets had any entry made while at head office — Mkhwanazi declined to give a percentage — and whether the five dockets with outstanding J50 arrest warrants suffered irremediable prejudice.
would_resolve: Production of the head-office audit itself, together with the handover registers bearing actual dates of physical transfer and return.

description: The PKTT's claimed effectiveness has not been substantiated in a form the Commission can use. The Chairperson pressed Mkhwanazi on Day 1 for a comparator against which the 'unmatched success rate' could be measured, questioned the raw docket-finalisation figures with Masemola on Day 4, and showed on Day 8 that Khumalo's figures do not reconcile (34 not guilty plus 82 withdrawn against 83 convictions). Adv Harrison offered on Day 7 to obtain historical and comparative finalisation and success-rate figures for PKTT prosecutions, but they were not produced.
would_resolve: Production of the comparative statistics Adv Harrison offered, and a corrected, case-level breakdown from Lt-Gen Khumalo distinguishing outcomes per accused from outcomes per case.

description: Witnesses B and C were provided for in the amended Day 15 ruling but had not testified by the end of Day 15. Witness B is referenced throughout Witness A's evidence as the co-investigator who was present at the Shibiri meeting, who declined to give a report over the phone, and to whom a senior officer at the second gathering allegedly 'made means to get through'.
would_resolve: The evidence of Witnesses B and C, which would test Witness A's account of the meeting, the gatherings and the approaches to the investigating team.

description: The 'three envelopes' bribery allegation remains untested and its chain of custody is unclear. Masemola relayed it as hearsay on Day 4 and pointed the Commission to General Khumalo, who did not address it on Days 8 or 9. Witness A gave first-hand evidence of it on Day 15, attributing it to Maj-Gen Shibiri. Masemola testified he does not know whether any case was opened on the allegation.
would_resolve: Evidence from Maj-Gen Shibiri, from Witness B (the co-investigator present at the meeting), and confirmation of whether any criminal or disciplinary case was registered.

description: Several people named in the chat evidence were never identified: 'Deon', who supplied PERSAL personnel and vehicle and address data to Mogotsi; 'Mr S', referenced in connection with animals kept at his plot; the 'Cele' whose contact card Maj-Gen Senona sent to Matlala; and the person referred to only as 'him' in an exchange about a complaint to the Minister via Mr Kareem. Whether 'Sibiya' and 'Khan' in particular chats refer to the SAPS officers of those names was described by the witness as inference, not established fact.
would_resolve: The supplementary statement Adv Hassim SC undertook on Day 12 to obtain, subscriber and metadata analysis, and the further evidence the witness said would be led in closed session.

description: Whether the identity behind the contact saved as 'Senzo Mchunu' on Brown Mogotsi's phone is in fact the Minister of Police has never been established. Mkhwanazi conceded on Day 3 that he cannot confirm it because neither Mogotsi's nor the Minister's handset had been examined by investigators, and the Day 9 chat evidence rests on the same saved-contact name. The identification of a voice in a social-media video clip as the Minister was likewise not independently verified.
would_resolve: Forensic examination of the handsets and subscriber records, or direct evidence from the Minister or Mr Mogotsi.

description: The Chairperson's question on Day 13 — what evidentiary value in-camera evidence carries if the parallel police investigations are not finalised before the Commission concludes, so that implicated persons never get to answer it — was met with an assurance rather than a mechanism. Adv Chaskalson SC said the Commission was 'hoping and confident' the situation would not arise and undertook that no findings would be made against any person on the basis of secret information that could not be put to them, but identified no fallback procedure.
would_resolve: A stated procedure for what happens to in-camera material that cannot be disclosed in time — for example a ruling that such evidence is excluded from the findings, or a mechanism for late disclosure and response.

description: Day 14 has no published transcript because the Commission ruled on Day 13 that the hearings on that day and the next would be held in camera, the media respondents having withdrawn their opposition. The substantive evidence of Day 13 was likewise heard in camera and is absent from the public record.
would_resolve: Public release of the in-camera transcripts once the underlying police investigations permit, as contemplated by the Day 12 ruling and by Adv Chaskalson SC's Day 13 undertaking that the material would become public before the Commission concludes its business.

description: The Minister's stated reason for disbanding the PKTT — that following an assessment it was 'no longer required nor adding any value' — was never explained. Masemola testified he repeatedly asked and does not know what assessment was performed, when, or by whom. The letter's recital that the PKTT was established following the Moerane Commission report was shown by two witnesses to be factually wrong, and no witness could account for how that claim entered the letter.
would_resolve: Evidence from the Minister, his Chief of Staff, or whoever drafted the letter, identifying the assessment relied on and the source of the Moerane recital.

description: Maj Gen Anthony Gopaul's affidavit — the source of the allegation that the Minister applied direct pressure over an iLembe councillor murder docket — was placed before the Commission unsigned on Day 3, with the Evidence Leaders stating they were trying to track down the signed original. It was never produced in Days 4 to 15, and Gopaul did not testify.
would_resolve: Production of the signed affidavit, or oral evidence from Maj Gen Gopaul, which would move the allegation from an unsigned document to tested testimony.

description: The IMC minutes said to corroborate the Inter-Ministerial Committee's approval of and support for the PKTT strategy were never produced. On Day 1 the Evidence Leader said a declassification process had been initiated; on Day 2 the position was unchanged. No IMC minutes appear anywhere in Days 3 to 15.
would_resolve: Completion of the declassification process and tender of the IMC minutes as an exhibit, which would test the witnesses' accounts of the executive mandate under which the PKTT was created and extended.

description: No implicated person had responded at the Commission by the end of Day 15. The Chairperson placed on record on Day 2 that, because the first witness statement was finalised the day before hearings began, implicated-person notices could not go out before testimony started, and directed that notices, transcripts and underlying statements be sent. On Day 8, when a fresh set of individuals was named (Mogotsi, Senona, Julius Mkhwanazi, Rafadi, Kareem, and by implication the Minister, his Chief of Staff and Lt Gen Sibiya), Adv Hassim SC confirmed notices had still not been issued but were in preparation.
would_resolve: Confirmation on the record of which notices were actually served and when, followed by Phase 2 of the Commission's stated three-phase process, in which implicated persons respond and cross-examination is permitted.

description: Day 164 — Tier 1 and Tier 2/3 conflict. The commission's own hearings index does NOT list a Day 164. Its most recent August entry is Day 163 on 20 August 2026. SABC News, SABC+ and YouTube all carry 'Day 164' material dated Friday 21 August 2026, and Tier 2/3 reporting describes Adams continuing his evidence that day. A sitting on 21 August is well attested. Whether it is numbered 164 is not confirmed by Tier 1, most likely because the commission's index had not yet been updated when it was read.
would_resolve: Re-reading the commission's hearings index after it publishes the 21 August entry.

description: Day 159 — Tier 1 and Tier 2/3 conflict. The commission's own hearings index records the Day 159 witness as 'Mr Carrim', with evidence leaders Adv Hassim SC and Adv Premhid. Tier 2 and Tier 3 reporting (TimesLIVE, Daily Maverick) says Carrim did NOT appear on 14 August and that the commission resolved to set a criminal process in motion over his non-compliance; a Sunday World item places Adv Drushantha Ramsamy at the commission that day. Adv Premhid is described in reporting as Carrim's counsel, not an evidence leader. Unresolved. The commission's index may be recording whose matter was before it rather than who took the stand. Both readings are held; neither is presented as settled.
would_resolve: The Day 159 transcript, downloadable from the commission's own page for 2026/08/14.

description: Tier 1 transcripts and audio exist for every sitting day and are downloadable from the commission's own per-day pages, but none has yet been read. Every day summary on this site still rests on Tier 2/3 reporting.
would_resolve: Downloading and reading the per-day transcripts, which would move day summaries, quotations and exhibit references from REPORTING to EVIDENCE.

description: The commission's index lists Day 154 (2026/08/05, Drushantha Ramsamy) and Day 153 (2026/08/04, Adv Peter Serunye), which this scaffold does not hold. The sample of ten days is therefore Days 155–164 by broadcaster numbering, which Tier 1 only confirms to 163.
would_resolve: Phase 2 back-fill from Day 1.

description: No formal exhibit numbering was recoverable except a single reference to a document marked 'A1'. Exhibit references are generally not carried in news reports.
would_resolve: Daily transcripts or the commission's exhibit bundle index.

description: The surname-only reference to the deceased taxi industry figure whose device evidence was led on Day 161 reflects an unresolved first-name conflict ('Jotham' vs 'Mswazi').
would_resolve: The commission's transcript for 18 August 2026, or a Tier 1/2 report giving the full name.

description: No sitting occurred on Saturday 22 August 2026. Matlala's evidence was scheduled to resume on Monday 24 and Tuesday 25 August 2026, and a filing deadline of 18:00 on 22 August was set, but these were future events not verified as having occurred.
would_resolve: Reporting from 24 August 2026 onward.

description: No photographs could be verified. Wikimedia Commons file pages and the Wikipedia API were not retrievable from this environment (Commons returned 'cache-only', the API returned HTTP 403, and Commons category/search pages required a permission grant). One Commons file page URL for Cyril Ramaphosa appeared verbatim in search results, but neither its licence nor a direct upload.wikimedia.org URL could be confirmed, so all photo fields are null.
would_resolve: A single fetch of the relevant Wikimedia Commons file pages (or the MediaWiki pageimages API) to read the direct file URL and licence template for each subject.

description: The commission's own site, criminaljusticecommission.org.za, is JavaScript-rendered. Its landing page fetched but returned no content; /about.php and /hearing.php returned 404. No official witness list, hearing calendar, transcript or exhibit index could be obtained from Tier 1.
would_resolve: Rendering the site with a headless browser, or locating the commission's PDF transcript/exhibit downloads or its media statements via a static endpoint.

description: Three of the six required status labels do not fit central non-witness, non-implicated public officials — notably President Cyril Ramaphosa, acting Minister of Police Firoz Cachalia, and acting National Commissioner Puleng Dimpane. They are therefore recorded only through the 'presidency' and 'ministry-of-police' org entries and in events, not in `people`.
would_resolve: Adding a neutral label such as 'Public official (not implicated)' to the closed list, or confirming whether any of them has given evidence to the commission.

description: The identities and institutional roles of the protected witnesses (Witness G, and the 'Witness X', 'Witness C', 'Witness E' and 'Witness F' referred to in reporting) are withheld, and Witness G's in-camera evidence is not public. Only Witness G could be included with enough sourcing.
would_resolve: Publication of a redacted transcript or a commission ruling describing each protected witness's role in general terms.

description: Full names for the nine Ekurhuleni officials and nine suspended SAPS bid-committee officers referred by the commission could not be verified. News24's summary named six Ekurhuleni officials (including Bafana Twala, Aiden McKenzie and Linda Gxasheka) but the retrieved text did not attribute a specific role or reason to each, so only the best-corroborated names were included.
would_resolve: Access to the full text of the first interim report, or a fully retrievable version of the Daily Maverick arrests list (2026-05-12), which was only partially readable.

description: Advocate Andrew Chauke, Gauteng South Director of Public Prosecutions, features in August 2026 evidence about an alleged IDAC/NPA probe into his communications, but the same source records that he was cleared by a fitness-for-office inquiry. Applying any 'Implicated' label from the closed list would misstate his position, so he is excluded from `people`.
would_resolve: Confirmation of whether the commission itself has made any adverse finding or invitation to respond regarding him.

description: Former Police Minister Bheki Cele appears in one secondary summary of Masemola's September 2025 testimony as having been implicated, but this rests on a single summarised bullet and could not be corroborated; his verified July 2026 testimony was to the separate Khampepe Commission, not this one. He is therefore excluded.
would_resolve: A transcript or direct-quote report of what Masemola said about Cele at the Madlanga Commission.

description: Wikipedia's Madlanga Commission article referred to a 'Witness D' identified as Marius van der Merwe, to a police informant named Jaco Hanekom, and to a 'Rovo Spies'. None of these could be corroborated in Tier 1–3 sources, so they were not carried into this roster.
would_resolve: Corroboration from commission transcripts or contemporaneous Tier 1–3 reporting.

description: Dates are approximate for a few entries: Rachel Matjeng's testimony is fixed only to February 2026, Julius Mkhwanazi's commission appearance to 14 April 2026 (inferred from a News24 headline slug rather than fetched body text), and the second interim report's delivery date (29 May 2026 per The Citizen) differs from the 6 August 2026 date on which the Presidency noted it.
would_resolve: The commission's published hearing calendar or the report cover dates.
